name: sqlx
description: SQLx 0.9.0 PostgreSQL driver on Tokio. explicit calls Pool::begin, Transaction::commit, and Transaction::rollback. managed calls Connection::transaction, which commits on Ok and calls rollback().await on Err. direct uses one PgConnection and the explicit calls, with no pool. drop and direct-drop drop an open Transaction instead of calling rollback(); Drop only queues ROLLBACK. sql sends SET TRANSACTION because begin has no isolation argument. The pool is PgPool, max_connections equal to pool_max, min_connections 0, test_before_acquire false. Category C faults are withheld or rewritten in this process, on the cleartext proxy in front of SQLx, once, before PostgreSQL receives the statement. Compile-time query macros are not enabled.

modes.description: PgPool begin, Transaction::commit, and Transaction::rollback. A nested Transaction::begin is SAVEPOINT _sqlx_savepoint_N. max_connections is pool_max, min_connections is 0, and test_before_acquire is false. No after_release hook is installed. SQLx still calls ping before returning a connection to the pool; that is the pool, not an adapter mitigation.

Connection::transaction on a connection checked out of the same PgPool. The callback's Ok commits and its Err calls rollback().await. A nested scope inside the callback is Transaction::begin, a savepoint. The pool settings match explicit.
One PgConnection, not a pool. begin, commit, and rollback are the explicit methods. TX-03 is not run: there is no pool to reuse. This separates SQLx's transaction result from PgPool's return path.

The same PgPool as explicit. Commit still calls Transaction::commit. Rollback paths drop the Transaction. Drop calls start_rollback, which queues the statement and does not wait. The pool's return path calls ping, which flushes that queue. TX-01A and TX-01B are not run: those cases end with COMMIT.

One PgConnection. CTL-01.rollback drops the Transaction and reports after-end before the connection is closed. No pool ping runs. Only the observation controls run, so a failed rollback control does not gate a scenario.

TX-05 only, plus the observation controls. begin and transaction take no isolation argument. The first statement is SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE. That is application SQL, not a transaction-API option. The explicit case then calls Transaction::commit. The managed case uses Connection::transaction.

TX-01B.commit-reply-discarded.reason: SQLx 0.9.0 PgConnection::run reads the simple-query response, including CommandComplete and ReadyForQuery, before Transaction::commit returns. There is no supported hook after that parse and before commit's Result where the adapter can discard a reply the driver has already accepted. The category E case, TX-01B.commit-reply-unseen, is the loss this adapter can run. This is not a claim that commit reports the command tag.

TX-04.independent-inner.reason: SQLx has no propagation mode that commits an inner transaction on a second connection while an outer transaction stays open. Transaction::begin on an open transaction is SAVEPOINT _sqlx_savepoint_N. Connection::transaction calls begin on the same connection. There is no deferred write queue. This adapter does not open a second connection and call it an independent transaction.
